summary: Parents talk of paying for college as a moral obligation, put off the money talk with the child, and keep the strain private.
realLife: A researcher who interviewed about 160 students and parents found families usually avoid the money talk with a child until a crisis forces it. Parents saw draining savings as proof they valued school, and called paying a moral obligation more than a budget problem. The strain is worked out privately, apart from the public arguments about tuition and debt.
sources: https://www.kuow.org/2019-09-17/what-the-strain-of-paying-for-college-does-to-families (public radio segment on a book about paying for college)
